review_notes: I read the whole file and its simp-relevant declarations. The simp lemmas are spectralSequencePageMap_f, spectralSequenceMap_hom, the _id and _comp lemmas for PageXMap, PageMap and spectralSequenceMap. Each rewrites a composite, or a projection of a bundled morphism, toward a canonical form built from the underlying components. Their left-hand sides are distinct, and the right-hand sides do not unfold the definitions. I found no competing rules and no credible cycle. The lemmas that carry heavy index data (spectralSequencePageXMap_eq, the PageXIso/EMap commutation lemmas, and the homology compatibility lemma) are left un-simp. That is correct, because their statements have many arbitrary index and equality arguments, and they are applied explicitly. The one stylistic point is that `@[reassoc, simp]` makes only the base lemma simp, not the reassoc form. The `(φ ≫ ψ)` lemmas rewrite subterms and then use Category.assoc, so this is not a defect. Mathlib's SpectralObject files use both `@[reassoc, simp]` (Page.lean:105) and `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` (Page.lean:219), so the file is not out of line. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out unnoticed simp-set interactions.
